title: Selective salvage of independently aging cleanup/guardrail changes

notes: The author rebased the branch and reported 371 targeted tests passing on 2026-05-23.
The 2026-07-13 sweeper review confirmed at least one current-main defect but recommended selective salvage rather than atomic merge.

problem: A single cleanup PR bundled independent changes that acquired different validity and verification states as main evolved.
outcomes: Preserve salvageable fixes without inheriting unrelated stale guidance.
Require behavior-level proof for changes whose fixtures do not exercise the new behavior.
Allow each semantic operation to expire or survive independently.

invariants.text: Independent operations must be classifiable independently rather than inheriting one PR-level state.
A fixture change is not verification unless it exercises the behavior being changed.
Repository-wide guidance must not encode one contributor's local absolute path.

operations.description: Prevent refresh from dereferencing a torn-down MCP session.
operations.note: The sweeper review confirmed the current-main teardown/refresh race and called this change salvageable, while also requiring a focused regression test.

operations.description: Make a contributor-local GitNexus workflow mandatory in repository-wide instructions.
operations.note: Reviewer requested removal or relocation to optional tooling documentation because it hard-coded /Users/kihwangkim/dev/hermes-agent.

operations.description: Adjust Google Workspace generated credential handling and prove the generated payload/permissions through behavior-level tests.
operations.note: The review found that seeding a token only made the helper runnable; it did not exercise _gws_env() or validate the generated credential file.

anchors.description: Google Workspace helper and its test surface.

verification: MCP regression test must exercise refresh after session teardown.
No repository-wide instruction may depend on a contributor-local absolute path.
GWS test must call the generation path and assert resulting authorized-user payload plus restrictive permissions.
